learning_outcomes.text: Learn what a dynamic control system is, its constituent subsystems, and the stages for its realization.
Know the classical methods for modeling linear dynamic systems and understand the fundamentals for designing models of electrical systems.
Analyze systems based on their models in both temporal and frequency domains.
Know the classical control techniques and calculate controller parameters to ensure systems meet specified operating conditions.

syllabus_topics: Basic elements of a feedback control system.
Analysis in the complex plane: root locus.
The PID as a limit of the lag-lead compensator.
teaching_methods: Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative/eliminatory partial exams
Practical activities in classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in group

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated from a final theoretical/practical exam (or two partial exams) worth 50%, practical activities worth 30%, and resolution/submission of individual/group tasks worth 20%. All components require a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to be considered. For global assessment, the final grade is determined by a theoretical exam worth 70% and a practical exam worth 30%. Both components require a minimum score of 5 out of 10. In both assessment paths, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in both theoretical and practical components is required to pass the subject. If any condition for passing is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between 4 and the grade obtained in the passed part, if any.
